content.text: Most tutorials about [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-building-crypto-store-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-explained-digital-5|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]]-pages-complete-infrastructure-4|building]] a digital store focus on the storefront. The storefront is the last thing you should configure. The backend is what makes the store work — and the backend is what most [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-creators-ghana-get-paid-online-everything-you-2|How Creators]] get wrong when they try to build without a clear sequence. In Stack 01, Google Apps Script serves as the backend Web App — it receives the NOWPayments webhook, validates the signature, confirms the transaction on-chain, logs the order to Google Sheets, and sends the delivery email via Gmail. In Stack 02, Cloudflare Workers replaces Apps Script with a faster, more scalable serverless backend that integrates natively with Supabase for order storage and Resend for email delivery. Configure the backend first, set the webhook endpoint URL in NOWPayments second, build the storefront third, and test on mainnet fourth.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

You don't need to rely on Stripe or other restricted payment platforms when you can build a sovereign crypto store on Cloudflare Pages. The combination of GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification provides a scalable and secure payment infrastructure that's not beholden to any single platform.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you deploy your sovereign crypto store, you'll need to choose between Stack 01 and Stack 02. Stack 01 is a more straightforward deployment that takes 4-6 hours and uses GitHub Pages for hosting and Apps Script for backend logic. Stack 02, on the other hand, is a more comprehensive deployment that takes 48 hours and uses Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Workers for backend logic, and Supabase for order storage.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to configure NOWPayments as your payment gateway. This involves integrating NOWPayments with your Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages site and setting up automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. You'll also need to configure Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, ensuring that your customers can download their purchased digital products without any issues.
You can deploy your sovereign crypto store in just 4-6 hours with Stack 01.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, it's time to go live and process your first transaction. This involves deploying your Stack 01 or Stack 02 infrastructure, configuring your payment gateway and file delivery settings, and testing your site to ensure that everything is working as expected. You can then process your first transaction and start selling your digital products to customers all over the world.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your sovereign crypto store is up and running, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to handle increased traffic and sales. This involves monitoring your site's performance, adjusting your payment and delivery pipeline as needed, and configuring your Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages site to handle increased traffic. You can also consider upgrading to Stack 02, which provides more comprehensive features and support for larger-scale deployments.

You can then configure NOWPayments as your payment gateway and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, ensuring that your customers can download their purchased digital products without any issues.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your sovereign crypto store, follow these steps: Choose between Stack 01 and Stack 02, set up your payment and delivery pipeline using NOWPayments and Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, deploy your site and configure your payment gateway and file delivery settings, test your site to ensure everything is working as expected, and scale your infrastructure as needed to handle increased traffic and sales. You can also consider upgrading to Stack 02 or the Edge Commerce Stack ($197) for more comprehensive features and support.
